_comment: `b.js` imports the CommonJS module `x.cjs`, then the lazy host `a.js`, then `y.js`. Native ESM runs `x` before `a`. In `esm` output, the file of `x.cjs` runs `x` at load, so the chunk of `b.js` initializes `a.js` right after its import of the host. In `cjs` output, `b.js` runs `x` in its body, at the read of the `default` export, so `b.js` keeps the call of `init_a()` in its body. `y.js` only gives the chunk of `b.js` a reason to initialize `a.js` at its import. It does not write to the log, and the test only checks that it runs.
